$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.36,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.36/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 726dcad8022f539d25ceaa3694471475e17e463e8d3aa194dc5e78a4cdef79d0 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.36/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
726dcad8022f539d25ceaa3694471475e17e463e8d3aa194dc5e78a4cdef79d0 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
